summary: Hyoscine butylbromide is a quaternary antimuscarinic that relaxes smooth muscle of the gastrointestinal, biliary and genitourinary tracts to relieve cramping/colicky pain and spasm. Being quaternary, it poorly crosses the blood-brain barrier so causes few central effects. It is not FDA-approved in the US; this record is based on the EMA/SmPC and BNF (Buscopan). Maximum recommended is generally 100 mg/day orally.
indications: Relief of gastrointestinal smooth-muscle spasm and colic
Spasm of the genitourinary tract (e.g. renal/ureteric colic) and biliary tract
Symptomatic relief of abdominal cramping in irritable bowel syndrome

dosage.d: 10-20 mg three to four times daily
20 mg IM or slow IV; may repeat after 30 minutes
dosage.n: Max ~100 mg/day; slow IV to limit hypotension/tachycardia

dosage.d: 10 mg three times daily; increase to 20 mg four times daily if needed

admin: Oral tablets swallowed whole with water, with or without food
Parenteral 20 mg may be given by slow IV injection or IM
Do not exceed approximately 100 mg in 24 hours
Have resuscitation available for IV use (rare anaphylaxis/cardiovascular effects)
moa: Hyoscine butylbromide is a quaternary ammonium antimuscarinic that competitively blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors on visceral smooth muscle and also has ganglion-blocking activity, relaxing smooth muscle of the gastrointestinal, biliary and urinary tracts and relieving spasm. Its quaternary structure limits CNS penetration.

absolute: Mechanical stenosis of the GI tract / paralytic ileus
relative: Prostatic enlargement with urinary retention risk

preg: Limited data. Use only if clearly necessary and the benefit justifies potential risk; antimuscarinics may affect the fetus/uterine activity.
lact: Limited data on excretion in milk; antimuscarinics can reduce milk production. Use with caution.
renal: No specific dose adjustment established; use with caution in severe impairment.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment established; use with caution in severe impairment.

major: Other anticholinergics (tricyclics, antihistamines, antipsychotics, antiparkinson agents) - additive antimuscarinic toxicity
moderate: Dopamine antagonists (metoclopramide, domperidone) - mutually antagonistic effects on GI motility
minor: Antacids may reduce absorption if taken together
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: No major interaction; both may cause mild drowsiness.
interactions.diagnostics: Reduces GI motility (useful for imaging); can raise heart rate.

monitoring: Anticholinergic effects - vision, urinary output, bowel function
Intraocular pressure in those at risk of glaucoma
counsel: This medicine relaxes gut/urinary spasm and eases cramping pain
Report eye pain, blurred vision with halos, or difficulty passing urine urgently
May cause dry mouth and a faster heartbeat
Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate or heart rhythm problems
Seek care if cramping pain is severe, persistent or with fever - it may need investigation
pk: Oral within ~15-30 min; IV within minutes
Plasma peak ~2 h after oral dosing
Several hours; dosed up to 4 times daily
Store below 25 C, protected from moisture and light
pearls: Quaternary structure means minimal CNS penetration - little sedation compared with tertiary antimuscarinics
Not FDA-approved in the US (marketed as Buscopan elsewhere); record based on EMA SmPC/BNF
Slow IV administration to reduce transient tachycardia and hypotension
Contraindicated in untreated narrow-angle glaucoma, myasthenia gravis and GI mechanical obstruction
Rare but serious anaphylaxis reported - keep resuscitation available for injections
missed: Take the missed dose when you remember unless it is nearly time for the next dose, then skip it. Do not take a double dose. As-needed dosing means only take it when you have symptoms.
overdose: Overdose causes anticholinergic features - dry mouth, tachycardia, urinary retention, blurred vision, flushing, and (rarely) CNS effects. Manage supportively; physostigmine may be considered for severe antimuscarinic toxicity, with urinary catheterisation and cardiac monitoring as needed.
